grain: one row per issued boil water advisory (labeled; censored and invalid-outcome rows excluded and counted)
eligibility: parseable issue date; issue date on or before the vintage minus 30 days (2026-05-17) so an unresolved advisory cannot masquerade as a negative; observed non-negative duration at the pinned vintage; three scored windows on issue year (train 2008-2017, eval 2018-2020, holdout 2021-2024)
label: lift30: advisory lifted within 30 days of issuance, from 'Date Advisory Removed'/'Length of Advisory in Days' (label-only columns, absent from the shipped files)

hazards_measured.same_site_issue_date_pairs: 19 pairs + 1 triple; 16 pairs have two valid durations (identical features, label noise, counted)
hazards_measured.duration_boundary: 16 rows at exactly 30 days (label 1), 6 at 31 (label 0), 14 at 29; 5 zero-duration rows
hazards_measured.reason_variant_merge: e. coli present 135 = 83 'E. Coli Present' + 52 'E.Coli Present'
hazards_measured.length_column_agreement: 0 disagreements between the register Length column and the recomputed duration
hazards_measured.regime_shift: mean advisory duration 47-65 days (2009-2018) vs 218 (2020), 143 (2021), 101 (2022), 64 (2023); the holdout window straddles the spike

references_eval_372_rows_225_positives.scope: identical eval rows (n=372), computed after gate PASS (44/44) and exact-byte --accept; holdout sealed

persistence_site_prior.definition: the site's as-of lift30 rate over earlier same-site advisories resolved strictly before the instant, RECOMPUTED REGISTER-SIDE post-acceptance (v2026.10 shipped this value as the site_prior_lift30_rate feature; v2026.12 removes that column and keeps the value as a reference only); the register fetch is asserted sha256-identical to the artifact's own vintage, so the reference reads no information the artifact's construction did not; global train rate fallback

calendar_county_month.definition: train-estimated (county, issue month) rate with >=5 train rows, county then global train rate backoff

reason_prior.definition: train-estimated positive rate per normalised reason

facility_prior.definition: train-estimated rate per facility type - constant scores on eval, no ranking information

persistence_vs_calendar.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

calendar_vs_reason.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

persistence_vs_reason.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

prevalence_shift_note: within-eval prevalence falls 0.7442 (2018) -> 0.64 (2019) -> 0.4153 (2020), the measured COVID-era duration regime shift; per-issue-year figures are mandatory reading beside the pooled AUC; persistence holds Brier 0.22-0.36 across the shift; prevalence drift does not by itself determine AUC
headroom_finding: NO demonstrated headroom under this protocol. The runner-contract model (0.5068) trails the register-side site-persistence reference (0.6124) by 0.1056 AUC on identical eval rows - the same honest expectation recorded before the rebuild, now a measured finding. No paired model-vs-persistence interval was recomputed for the v2026.12 frame; on these same eval rows the v2026.10 per-row diagnostic (ns-bwa-diag-001, 19-column frame, model 0.5086) measured the analogous deficit at -0.1038 with row-level interval [-0.1693, -0.0357] and site-clustered interval [-0.1706, -0.0383], both excluding zero, and the v2026.12 observed gap is larger. The model sits at the calendar/identity control level (0.5075). This is a recorded defect, not an encouraging result: no figure from this artifact may be quoted without this comparison beside it. It does not prove every competent model must lose; it says the runner's own baseline does not demonstrate the task's discriminative claim above simple references.
